boundaries_recorded_not_hidden: InternalMessageService.HandleAuthorize itself is not executed: it depends on *data.Authenticator, whose access-token path needs the Redis-backed user token cache, so a unit test would need a production seam that is out of scope. Its rule (token decides the user id, ?stream= must name that same user) is asserted at the transport boundary through TestHTTPStreamHandlerTwoUserStreamIsolation, and the authorize/subscribe hooks are proven to be the ones NewSseServer injects.

A periodic entry registered while the transport is not Started never fires, because WithRedisURI creates but does not run the scheduler; that is v1.3.14 behaviour and is unchanged. The business acceptance therefore starts the server, exactly as the production wiring order does.
asynq's Inspector.SchedulerEntries() reports nothing for in-process registrations here, so periodic registration is proven through entry IDs plus real firings rather than through the Inspector.
Same-stream slow-subscriber coupling is recorded as an observation (the dispatch loop blocks on a full subscriber and the rest of the stream queues) and is not turned into a new contract.
